clue.text: Reliable PC offered to journalist with Basic installed

indicators.note: installed says one piece is set inside the others, here between the policeman and the editor

parts.note: a police constable is a copper
ED is the crossword editor, a journalist
the bottom of something is its basic, fundamental level

explanation.surface: A dependable police officer gives a reporter some help with a computer language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic' looks like the programming language but means fundamental; 'installed' sets it between the policeman and the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something copper-bottomed is thoroughly safe and trustworthy, from ships' hulls sheathed with copper.

clue.text: Having bombs, airmen fail to hit islands, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: aircrews miss isles: airmen are crews, fail to hit is miss, islands are isles

explanation.surface: Bomber crews carrying their payload fail to strike their island targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link; 'crews miss isles', said out loud, gives the weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruise missiles are guided flying bombs carrying explosive warheads.

clue.text: Notice new rear entrance

parts.note: a poster is a public notice

explanation.surface: A sign announces a fresh back door.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a back or side gate, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: In English literature there's place for old poet

indicators.note: there's place for says room is made inside for another piece

explanation.surface: English literature makes room for a poet of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's place for' puts O inside LIT, after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: T S Eliot wrote The Waste Land, and George Eliot was a novelist who also wrote verse.

clue.text: Rail hold-up and bus alert after crash

indicators.note: after crash says the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A railway holdup and a bus warning follow an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail hold-up' suggests a train robbery; it is a support holding up a handrail.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short posts that hold up the rail of a staircase or balustrade.

clue.text: Given order by troop leader, I departed

indicators.note: leader says take the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: departed is a euphemism for died

explanation.surface: A soldier says he left after his commanding officer gave instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given order' suggests a command; here it means made orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy is to put in order, so tidied means given order.

clue.text: Mature students prepared this MA after work, and succeeded

indicators.note: after says the anagram follows the work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: prepared says the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Older students got a master's degree ready after their work, and passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' shuffles 'this MA'; 'after' puts the result behind the work. An opsimath is a rare word for a late learner.
explanation.definitionFit: An opsimath is someone who begins learning late in life, a mature student.

clue.text: In cryptic version, crosswords often will be started and completed outside

indicators.note: outside says the completed word goes round the other letters

parts.note: completed means ended

indicators.note: will be started says only the starts of the words before are used

explanation.surface: Crosswords are often begun and finished in a coded version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be started' takes C and O from 'crosswords often'; ENDED goes 'outside' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something encoded has been put into a cipher, a cryptic version of the original.

clue.text: Still be shocked? Remain calm!

definitions.meaning: to be shocked can mean to have hair standing on end, but not lose it
a British idiom urging someone not to lose their temper

explanation.definitionFit: Keep your hair on is British slang for stay calm, and literally means keep one's hair attached despite a fright.

clue.text: Clumsy German tribesmen losing leader, murdered

indicators.note: losing leader says the tribesmen's word drops its opening letter

parts.note: the Huns were a warlike tribe, and 'Huns' is old slang for Germans
murdered means killed

explanation.surface: Inept Germanic warriors, deprived of their chief, are slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing leader' takes the H off HUNS, leaving UNS.
explanation.definitionFit: An unskilled worker lacks training and expertise, so is clumsy or inexpert at the job.

clue.text: First to swap unusual coins regularly, exchanging this currency?

definitions.text: First to swap unusual coins regularly, exchanging this currency?

indicators.note: First to says take the opening letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: Someone eager to change odd coins asks which currency they belong to.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'swap unusual coins regularly, exchanging' spell the answer, and the whole clue nods to the currency being swapped for the US dollar in 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: The sucre was Ecuador's currency until the country switched to the US dollar in 2000.

clue.text: Bridge partners set about winning

indicators.note: about says the word set goes round the partners

parts.note: taken as written
at bridge West and East play as partners, W and E

explanation.surface: A pair of card players set out to win their game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' looks like part of the bridge story; it is the definition, in the sense of charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning manner is a charming, engaging one, and sweet means charming or lovable.

clue.text: Vegetables finally combined together in a stew

indicators.note: finally says take the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: to team up is to combine, so combined together means teamed up

explanation.surface: Root vegetables are thrown in together to make a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes 'stew' a dish; here 'in a stew' means agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew is an idiom for being anxious or agitated, which is what steamed up means.

clue.text: Cash secures short period of time here in California

indicators.note: secures means holds inside, so the cash word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: short says the word for the period loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period of time, such as a school term

explanation.surface: Money buys a brief spell somewhere on the Californian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter from the period of time; 'secures' has the cash hold what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Monterey is a coastal city in California, so it names a place there.

clue.text: Gym member cut out runs without a word of hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the cut word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
er is the sound of hesitation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A gym-goer gets cut from the running without a word of hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the cut-out word and the runs go round the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exerciser is someone who works out, as a gym member does.

clue.text: I'll follow boss round workplace

parts.note: a boss is a raised ornamental stud or knob
the I of the clue, which will follow
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: An employee promises to tour the office behind the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager, but here it is an ornamental knob, a stud; I then comes after it, and O for 'round' ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist, photographer or broadcaster does their work.

clue.text: Head of bank phones concerning advances

indicators.note: Head of says take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to ring is to phone
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A bank manager telephones about loans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' suggests loans; here it is a verb meaning promotes or brings forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring on is to advance or help develop something, such as a young player.

clue.text: Private Eye lovers put in new order

indicators.note: put in new order says the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Readers of the satirical magazine Private Eye are reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine, but here a private eye is a detective, one who solves cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A private investigator works out crimes, so he is a solver of mysteries.

clue.text: Salad dishes, some rejected? That's typical of boys

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Turning up your nose at salad is just what boys do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks out letters running across 'Salad dishes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish behaviour is boisterous and typical of young men, like spurning greens.

clue.text: At end of working week, sportsman becomes more lively

parts.note: Friday, abbreviated FRI, ends the working week
a skier is a sportsman

explanation.surface: Come Friday, an athlete perks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and energetic, so the comparative is livelier.

clue.text: Special knowledge of local area among reporters

indicators.note: among reporters says the words are heard as spoken

parts.note: something of the local area is on the spot, in site

explanation.surface: Journalists have inside knowledge of the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in site' means belonging to the area; said out loud it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep understanding or special knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Cheap containers

parts.note: a tin is a container
a pot is a container

explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot means inferior or worthless, as in a tinpot dictator.

clue.text: Reasoning with logic it's a sort of motor

definitions.meaning: inferring general rules from particular cases is a form of logical reasoning
an electric motor driven by electromagnetic currents is so named

explanation.surface: Someone explains logical reasoning by comparing it to an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Induction is both inference from examples and the electromagnetic principle behind a common motor.

clue.text: Crush a high-ranking officer

parts.note: a pash is British slang for an infatuation or crush

explanation.surface: Someone is infatuated with a senior military man.
explanation.walkthrough: PASH is dated British slang for a schoolgirl crush.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a senior officer or governor in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Portion of tart and cake with no filling

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie

indicators.note: with no filling says only the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: A slice of tart and a cake with nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no filling' keeps the C and E of 'cake'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion of something, such as a slice of cake.

clue.text: Priest — a saint and prophet

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A list of holy men: a cleric, a saint and a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet.

clue.text: Traveller, westward bound, about to take break touring Scottish loch

indicators.note: westward bound in an across clue means the letters run right to left

parts.note: about means concerning, RE

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the break word encloses the loch

parts.note: a gap is a break
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish loch

clue.text: Star player in soccer club: he's not for transfer

parts.note: Charlton Athletic is a London football club

indicators.note: for transfer says the letters are moved about, as a footballer is transferred
